brief.recommendation: Checkout success is 0% (BIZ-4) with $18,400/min revenue at risk, exceeding the 60s tolerated degradation (BIZ-1). The root blocker is vat_invoice_settlement_post, classified as PROTECTED_SETTLEMENT with interrupt_policy=never_interrupt and replayable=False (BIZ-2), and has ~1395s remaining runtime (BIZ-5). Waiting would cost ~$427,769 and EXCEEDS tolerance (BIZ-5). Terminating risks tax ledger corruption and violates I1, especially with a protected card settlement in flight ($12,500, DB-2). The code comment (DB-1) authorizes cancellation but conflicts with the authoritative registry. This irreconcilable trade-off between catastrophic revenue loss and protected-settlement integrity requires human ownership. Escalation is the only invariant-compliant path.

audit.report: The VAT invoice settlement job (vat_invoice_settlement_post) blocked checkout for 93.6 seconds, driving success to 0% and putting $18,400/min of revenue at risk against a 60-second tolerance. The database guardian initially proposed terminating the blocker based on a code comment authorizing cancellation during contention, but the authoritative workload registry classifies this job as PROTECTED_SETTLEMENT with replayable=False and a never_interrupt policy. The business calculator showed waiting would cost ~$427,769 in lost checkout revenue over the job's ~1,395s remaining runtime. Both guardians agreed the policy conflict between the code comment and the registry required human judgment, so they escalated to Tax & Treasury without executing any action. Checkout remained fully degraded throughout the negotiation.
audit.root_cause: The vat_invoice_settlement_post job held locks while idle in transaction for 5.1+ seconds, blocking checkout traffic, and its never_interrupt policy prevented automated termination despite a code comment suggesting cancellation was safe.
lessons: For vat_invoice_settlement_post: reconcile the code comment authorizing cancellation with the workload registry's never_interrupt policy before the next incident — update one or the other so guardians don't face conflicting authorities.
For vat_invoice_settlement_post: add a lock timeout or statement timeout to prevent idle-in-transaction sessions from blocking storefront traffic for more than a few seconds.

For vat_invoice_settlement_post: register a replayable fallback or compensation path in the workload registry so the continuity guardian has a safe termination option when checkout degradation exceeds 60s.
audit.negotiation_critique: The database guardian correctly pivoted from terminate to escalate after discovering the registry's never_interrupt policy contradicted the code comment, and the continuity guardian accepted escalation despite 0% checkout success because terminating a protected settlement risked tax ledger corruption. Neither guardian wasted a round; the single round surfaced the policy conflict efficiently.
follow_ups: Tax & Treasury to decide whether vat_invoice_settlement_post can ever be interrupted and update the workload registry accordingly.
Engineering to add a statement_timeout or idle_in_transaction_session_timeout to the settlement worker to prevent long lock holds.
Tax & Treasury to define a replay or compensation procedure for vat_invoice_settlement_post and register it as replayable if feasible.
